prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” roofing company that’s right for everyone — the best choice depends on your exact location in Dallas, roof size and pitch, materials you want, budget, whether the job is storm damage/insurance-related, and your tolerance for risk. Instead of one name, I recommend this quick plan to find the best roofer for your replacement:

What to do now
- Get 3 written estimates from different local contractors. Compare scope (decking repair, underlayment, ventilation), materials, start/completion dates, cleanup, and total price.
- Verify each contractor’s insurance (liability and workers’ comp) and request the carrier name and policy number.
- Check online ratings and reviews: Google, BBB, and recent customer photos. Ask for at least 3 local references and call them.
- Confirm they pull required permits and provide a written contract detailing materials, manufacturer and workmanship warranties, payment schedule, and a lien waiver at final payment.
- Prefer contractors who are manufacturer-certified (examples: GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred, CertainTeed Select). That affects material warranties and installer workmanship coverage.

Important questions to ask each roofer
- Are you licensed to work in Dallas/City of Dallas permits required?
- What brand and class of shingles do you recommend (and why)?
- How long will the job take? How many crew members will be on site?
- How do you handle hidden deck damage? How will change orders be billed?
- Do you provide a written warranty for workmanship and what does it cover?

Red flags
- Pressure to sign immediately or demands for large up-front cash payments.
- No local references or physical business address.
- Poor communication or vague scope/contract language.

If you want, I can:
- Shortlist 4–6 top-rated roofers in your specific Dallas ZIP code
- Prepare an interview checklist you can print and use on-site

Tell me your ZIP code, roof type (asphalt shingle, tile, metal), and whether this is insurance-related and I’ll pull a tailored short list and next steps.
